sections.title: Scenario
sections.prompt: Who is the user, what is the job, and which numbers shape the design?
criteria: States the user and the job in one sentence
Derives daily volume and the webinar-spike rate from the prompt
Names a pipeline metric (such as opportunities per 1,000 leads) with a baseline and target
Lists at least one thing explicitly out of scope

sections.title: Single View
sections.prompt: Draw the system as layers: what runs in each, what it hands to the next, and why it exists.
criteria: Has separate layers for dedupe, enrichment, scoring, routing and CRM write-back
Shows the score computed by code, separate from the model step
States one idea that separates what the model does from what code decides

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.prompt: Which sources feed the agent, what does each cost, and how fresh must each be?
criteria: Lists form, CRM, company enrichment, person enrichment and website as distinct sources
States an assumed per-lookup price for enrichment
Gates the expensive lookups (for example person enrichment only for high tiers)
Checks the live CRM before writing, not only a cached copy

sections.title: Processing
sections.prompt: How do raw form text, website pages and vendor data become features?
criteria: Normalises domains and bands employee counts in code
Has the model output fixed enums or a schema, not a free-form score
Validates model output and names a fallback when it fails

sections.title: Agents
sections.prompt: Is this an agent or a workflow, and what bounds each model step?
criteria: Uses a fixed workflow with steps in code
Gives model steps no write or paid tools, or justifies any it has
Makes steps resumable so a retry skips completed work
States a time or call limit per lead

sections.title: Memory
sections.prompt: What does the system keep between leads, where, and for how long?
criteria: Caches company enrichment by domain with an expiry
Logs features, score and model version for every lead
Handles deletion of personal data on opt-out

sections.title: MCP Tool Servers
sections.prompt: Which tools exist, with what arguments, and what does each enforce?
criteria: Lists each tool and whether it reads, writes or spends money
Enforces enrichment spend caps inside the tool server with numbers
Checks consent and region before person enrichment in code
Makes CRM writes idempotent on an external id

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.prompt: What is the API surface, and how is the speed-to-lead budget spent?
criteria: Verifies webhook signatures and acknowledges before doing the work
Splits speed to lead by stage and the total fits 5 minutes
Prioritises demo requests over other leads (separate queue or priority)
Shows the webinar spike can be drained with the stated worker count

sections.title: Caching
sections.prompt: What do you cache, what does it save, and what is the monthly cost?
criteria: Gives a monthly cost table covering both LLM and enrichment calls
Shows enrichment, not tokens, is the dominant cost
Coalesces or caches lookups for repeated domains
Does not cache the score itself

sections.title: Data Stores
sections.prompt: Which stores hold what, how big are they, and how do you stop duplicate accounts?
criteria: Names each store with what it holds and a size estimate
Matches accounts by normalised domain plus a fuzzy name match
Prevents concurrent leads from one company creating two accounts (lock or equivalent)
Keeps Salesforce as the system of record

sections.title: Output
sections.prompt: What does each audience receive, and which parts come from the model versus code?
criteria: Writes to agent-owned CRM fields and fills standard fields only when empty
Derives score reasons from the scoring model, not model prose
Checks facts in the brief against the enrichment payload

sections.title: Guardrails
sections.prompt: For each rule protecting money, permissions or privacy, what enforces it if the model ignores instructions?
criteria: Uses a least-privilege CRM integration user with field-level limits
Excludes protected attributes from scoring with an allowlist in code
Treats form text and web pages as untrusted data that cannot set the score
Redacts PII from logs or traces

sections.title: Key Impact
sections.prompt: What business number moves, and how do you prove the agent caused it?
criteria: Uses a concurrent holdout to attribute lift
Checks score calibration with a named measure and target
Tracks rep trust (reassign or disqualify rate)
Translates the result into hours or pipeline

sections.title: Failure Modes
sections.prompt: What breaks, and what catches each failure?
criteria: Covers an enrichment vendor outage with a partial score
Covers CRM lock or rate-limit errors with idempotent retries
Covers score drift with a named monitor and threshold
Covers a rep who never picks up the lead

sections.title: Build Order
sections.prompt: In what order do you build it, and what number unlocks each step?
criteria: Builds labelled history and a golden set first
Runs scoring in shadow before reps see tiers
Ends each step with a measurable number
Rolls out CRM writes gradually (sandbox, then a percentage)
